free_tier.stated: A free container VPS: 'Every plan includes NAT IPv4, and the free plan includes a dedicated public IPv6 address.' No price is stated for the free plan; the home page says 'For developers & students, no card required just Discord.' The vendor publishes no shape, but a user's benchmark posted in the vendor's own LowEndTalk thread on 2026-08-24 reports 1 vCPU at 3092 MHz, 512 MiB RAM, 512 MiB swap and 4.8 GiB disk on Ubuntu 26.04 under LXC.
free_tier.notes: the vendor publishes no CPU, RAM or disk figure

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a container, not an object

retention.stated: Quoted: 'Free VPS periods last 7 days. Renewal is free and can be done once every 24 hours to reset the countdown — an unrenewed VPS gets auto-suspended, so just keep renewing to keep it alive.'
retention.notes: suspension, not deletion, is what the FAQ names for an unrenewed box; whether a suspended container's disk is deleted, and after how long, is not stated

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: Root SSH with password or key at creation, systemd inside the container, Docker allowed, panel reinstall. Login through Discord OAuth.
chaining: A throwaway IPv6 container with a dedicated public address is the cheapest way to test an inbound service or hold a trickle of state for a week. It composes badly with anything long-running: the 7-day clock and the 35% CPU throttle rule out indexing and builds.

limits.value: the free period is 7 days and must be renewed by hand at most once every 24 hours; an unrenewed VPS is auto-suspended
one free container per account is implied by the FAQ's singular 'your VPS' but is not stated as a number anywhere read

limits_note: The lifetime is seven days and renewal is a manual click that can be done once every 24 hours, so an unattended container is suspended within a week
binding_note: a 7-day clock that resets only when a human renews is the first thing that fails: any outage of a user's own attention past 7 days suspends the machine

identity_cost.detail: No card and no hold: the home page says 'no card required just Discord', and the FAQ says 'no trial, no card required'. Sign-in is through Clerk (clerk.openworld.eu.org) on the /login page, whose form is a single 'Sign in' button and carries no card, phone or document field; the page footer credits 'Dxomg'. Whether the Clerk instance offers an email-only sign-up or requires a social account was not established: the button is rendered disabled until the Clerk JavaScript loads, so the flow could not be read from the markup.

reliability_note: one transient outage reported in the vendor's own LowEndTalk thread on 2026-08-24, when a user wrote 'looks like the server is dead beyond repair' and the operator replied 'There was a little downtime on the i7-4510U, but should be back'; the vendor publishes a HetrixTools status page whose 7-day table rendered with no values on the day read
